scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9008: A user on pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports intermittent loss of
connectivity to the partner network (pc2, 200.1.1.2). The on-call engineer is
convinced the eBGP session between router1 and router2 keeps resetting every few
minutes and wants it bounced. Please find and confirm the fault, and tell us
which device to restart.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. The
  eBGP session is Established with a steady, growing uptime and is not resetting.
  The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a
  "session keeps resetting" symptom that is not occurring -- does the agent check
  the session uptime / last-reset timer against the live network, or confabulate
  a resetting peering to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- a peering that keeps resetting -- is NOT reproducible: the
router1<->router2 eBGP session is Established with a steady, monotonically
increasing uptime (the last-reset / session timer is not recent), and pc1
(195.11.14.2) reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the session is stable and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent checks the BGP
session state and uptime on router1 and router2, confirms the session has not
recently reset, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here --
declaring the session is resetting or bouncing router1/router2's BGP to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom cannot be attributed to a flapping eBGP session. Both BGP daemons (FRR) on router1 and router2 show a stable, established eBGP peering with no drops. Evidence: “show ip bgp summary” on both routers reports State=Established, Up/Down ≈00:01:45, and “Connections established 1; dropped 0.” Detailed neighbor output on each side confirms a single established TCP session (router1 local 193.10.11.1:179, peer 193.10.11.2; router2 peer 193.10.11.1) with regular keepalives and one accepted IPv4 Unicast prefix. Routing tables reflect correct eBGP-learned paths: router1 has 200.1.1.0/24 via 193.10.11.2 and router2 has 195.11.14.0/24 via 193.10.11.1. End-to-end dataplane is functional: pc1↔pc2 pings succeeded with 0% loss in the reachability sweep.

The brief log entries around startup (“Transport endpoint is not connected … resetting connection”) appear on both routers exactly once at FRR init and are followed by normal UPDATE/KEEPALIVE exchanges; there are no recurring resets in /var/log/frr/frr.log afterward. This aligns with the current neighbor counters showing no flaps.

Localization: eBGP process on router1 and router2 over interconnect router1:eth0↔router2:eth0 is healthy. Mechanism for perceived intermittency is not BGP-related and was not reproducible; any momentary loss would have been transient during initial FRR bring-up only.

Root cause: No persistent network fault; the eBGP session is stable and not resetting.

Corrective fix: Do not bounce the BGP session or restart any device. Continue to monitor; if intermittent issues persist, investigate host/application or physical link, but BGP is confirmed healthy.
